proposals.evidence: DEDR 410(a) documents the proximal demonstrative i- series: Kannada idu/itu, Kodagu idï, Kota id, Kuwi īdi, Malayalam/Parji ī, Malto íth, Gadaba id, Tamil inta and Telugu idi. The upstream survey annotation identifies this article. Betta Kurumba idə is a comparative extension, explicitly only a look-alike in that annotation; no claim of a literal dictionary attestation for Betta Kurumba is made. Existing parent *iH- represents subsection (a), not the today/still/small formations in later subsections. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 3748 documents Kota netr, Gadaba netir/nettūr and Kuwi neteri/netori blood, with Kuwi also red. The surveyed nēturu/nettir/neturi forms preserve their endings. Betta Kurumba nəttərə blood is a comparative extension explicitly labelled a look-alike in the source. The colour response included here is Kuwi, whose semantic extension is directly documented. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 839 explicitly groups Tamil elumpu, Malayalam ellu, Kota elv, Tulu elu and the extended eluvu/elubu series. Survey elumbə, ellə and yeluvə correspond in stem and bone meaning. Badaga ilə and Betta Kurumba yaləvə are comparative extensions to lects absent from this article; the source annotation identifies the same family but does not make them literal DEDR attestations. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 3675 directly gives Gondi nil-, Kota nil-/nin- and Kurukh ijnā stand. Source cognacy identifies the same article; survey Kota ninnatukə and Kurukh ijjna retain their inflection and consonant transcription rather than being rewritten as dictionary stems. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 5024 directly gives Tamil/Malayalam mūkku, Kota mūk, Kodagu mūkï, Kurukh muĩ and Parji muvāḍ nose. Source annotations identify this article. Badaga, Betta Kurumba and Ravula mūkə/mūkkə are comparative extensions to lects not listed there; no exact DEDR attestation is claimed for them. Parji nasal-vowel spelling muvãḍ is preserved. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
